We have list of templates. Need the one that when applied to the molecule below reproduces electrophilic bromination. Which template is appropriate? The first entry reaction_id 1141 has retro_smarts_template: '[Br;H0;D1;+0:1]-[c;H0;D3;+0:3](:[c:2]):[c:4]>>Br-[Br;H0;D1;+0:1].[c:2]:[cH;D2;+0:3]:[c:4]'. That seems to be a retro template that breaks C-Br bond to give Br-Br and aromatic H. Forward would be Br-Br + aromatic H -> aromatic Br + Br? Actually forward: Br-[c] -> Br-Br + aromatic? Not sure. The mapped_rxn given is weird includes many other groups. Might be not correct.

We need mapped_rxn associated with the template that reproduces the reaction. Likely the simplest template: aromatic bromination. The template ID (template_id) is integer, not hash. In results we have reaction_id field maybe corresponds to template_id? The task says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash)". So likely reaction_id is the template ID. So we can pick the first template with reaction_id 1141. Provide its mapped_rxn.

Thus answer: {'mapped_rxn': 'Br[Br:5].Br.[CH3:1][C:2]1=[CH:3][CH:4]=[C:6]([CH3:7])[CH:8]=[CH:9]1>>[CH3:1][C:2]1=[CH:3][C:4]([Br:5])[C:6]([CH3:7])[CH:8]=[CH:9]1', 'template_id': 1141}

Check that mapped_rxn is from entry. Yes.

Return JSON.
